title: Multi‐energy microgrids for integrated renewable water supply in off‐grid regions
content:
Abstract

Reliable access to clean water and electricity remains a dangerous challenge for off-grid and remote regions, mainly in areas with harsh climatic conditions. This study presents a multi-energy microgrid framework that incorporates renewable energy generation with water pumping and treatment systems to address the water–energy nexus in resource-constrained communities. A hybrid solar photovoltaic (18 kWp) and wind (10 kW) energy system, reinforced by 40 kWh battery storage and 25 m3 water storage, is modeled and improved for a high-altitude case study in Ladakh, India. An Integrated Renewable Water-Energy Optimization (IRWEO) framework is recognized to equally accomplish energy and water demands, while a Dynamic Storage and Pumping Management (DSPM) strategy schedules battery use and water pumping based on renewable availability and demand predictions. The improved microgrid delivers 50.4 kWh/day electricity and 2.9 m3/day water with 99.1% reliability, accomplishing 97% renewable energy penetration, reducing CO2 emissions by 93.8%, and preserving a levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) of USD 0.19/kWh. Hourly simulations over 1 year, combined with sensitivity and ablation analyses, authorize the robustness of the framework under ±20% variation in solar and wind resources and ±30% variation in battery costs. These results authorize improved renewable utilization, reduced operational costs, and high water supply reliability compared to conventional hybrid microgrid configurations. The recommended framework proposes a scalable and sustainable solution for integrated energy–water arrangement in off-grid regions. Future work will discover AI-based predictive control, hydrogen storage, and demand-side management to further enlarge system efficiency, resilience, and sustainability.
